J&K Police Bust ISI-Linked Digital Spy Network in Kathua

#Jammu and Kashmir #ISI #Espionage #Cybersecurity

Jammu and Kashmir Police have successfully dismantled a digital espionage network allegedly operated by Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) in the Kathua district. The operation led to the arrest of a 24-year-old truck driver who is suspected of being a key operative in the network.

According to investigative reports, the suspect was reportedly recruited through 'honey-trapping' techniques. Once established, the operative was provided with specialized hardware to facilitate digital spying operations. This equipment was intended to collect sensitive information and transmit it back to handlers in Pakistan.

The police investigation suggests that the network utilized a combination of psychological manipulation and sophisticated hardware to bypass local security measures. The arrest marks a significant breakthrough in the region's ongoing efforts to counter cross-border digital threats and intelligence gathering.

Authorities are currently analyzing the seized hardware and digital devices to determine the full extent of the data breach and to identify any other potential accomplices involved in the ring. The investigation remains ongoing as security agencies intensify their surveillance of digital communication channels in the area.

What to watch: The extent of the data compromised and whether additional sleeper cells are identified through forensic analysis.
